Hi Alice — thanks for the clear ask. Short answer up front: Redwood does not use customer prompt or response content to train our public or internal models as part of our standard product offering. Below I’ve sketched the practical nuances and retention windows so your security team has what it needs. Happy to jump on a quick call if useful.

What we do NOT do (standard policy, hosted plans):
- We do not add customer prompt/response text to model training datasets.
- We do not surface customer data to other customers.

Runtime artifacts and retention (hosted):
- Billing/usage logs (token counts, timestamps): retained 90 days for billing and analytics, then aggregated to anonymized metrics.
- Structured telemetry (latency, error codes, model variant): retained 180 days for SLA monitoring and performance analysis.
- Debug snapshots / ephemeral traces: generated only when a request triggers an internal debug flow (e.g., runtime exception, reproducibility investigation). These are short-lived and stored encrypted; default retention is 7 days and they are purged automatically. Debug snapshots are not used for model training.
- KV cache / prefix caches: ephemeral; caches are quarantined per-request and not persisted to training pipelines; eviction policies typically expire entries in 0–24 hours depending on load.

Private & Dedicated options:
- Dedicated: customer data stays in your reserved capacity pool. We can configure longer or shorter debug snapshot retention per contract and provide attestations.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): no data leaves your environment and Redwood control plane only sees metadata; training/use-by Redwood does not occur.

Evidence and next steps:
- Attached: redwood-no-train-assurance.pdf (short attestation) and retention-matrix-summary.csv.
- We can add a specific DPA/Datasheet clause for "no training on customer data" and specify retention windows in SOW/contract language.

Let me know if your security team needs the SOC 2 artifact bundle or a call with our infra team to walk through the debug snapshot lifecycle.

Best,

Mina — quick confirmation from infra/legal side:
- Debug snapshots: default retention is 7 days. Snapshots are redacted where possible (PII patterns are removed using automated scrubbing), encrypted at rest, and purged automatically. For Dedicated customers we can shorten to 0 days or keep an audit-only retention per contract.
- KV caches / prefix caches: eviction policy is workload dependent; typical TTL is under 24 hours. Caches are never dumped into long-term storage and are disallowed from being used in training pipelines.
- Billing/observability logs: 90 days raw, then aggregated/anonymized for long-term metrics.

If FinHealth needs contractual language, we should offer: (a) explicit no-training clause, (b) debug snapshot max retention = 7 days (with option to set to 0), and (c) statement that KV caches are excluded from training. We can provide SOC 2 artifacts and an engineer walkthrough on the snapshot lifecycle.
